scenarios.name: single, age 60, below the 62 floor: no retirement income exclusion
scenarios.source: 2025 IT-511 Individual Income Tax Instruction Booklet (https://dor.georgia.gov/document/document/2025-it-511-individual-income-tax-booklet/download), page 21, 'Subtractions', item 1 'Retirement income': 'The maximum retirement income exclusion is $35,000 for taxpayers who are: A. 62 - 64 years of age, or B. less than 62 and permanently disabled...The maximum retirement income exclusion is $65,000 for taxpayers who are 65 years of age or older.' Age 60, not disabled, qualifies for neither tier, so the exclusion is $0. Single filer, pension income $20,000, federalAGI $20,000. Georgia standard deduction for TY2026 is $15,000 single (Georgia DOR, 'Important Tax Updates', https://dor.georgia.gov/taxes/important-tax-updates: 'The Georgia standard deduction has been increased to $15,000 for single taxpayers...or $30,000 for married taxpayers filing jointly'), effective retroactive to 01/01/2026 under HB 463. Gov. Kemp's own signing announcement (https://gov.georgia.gov/press-releases/2026-05-11/gov-kemp-signs-legislation-lowering-taxes-and-supporting-economic-growth) names the bill directly: 'HB 463 lowers Georgia's state income tax rate from 5.19% to 4.99%, beginning January 1, 2026,' signed May 11, 2026. Georgia taxable income = 20000-15000-0 = 5000. Georgia's TY2026 flat rate is 4.99% (same DOR important-tax-updates page: 'The Georgia income tax rate has been reduced to a flat rate of 4.99%.'). Tax = 5000*0.0499 = $249.50.

scenarios.name: single, age 63, squarely in the 62-64 tier: $35,000 exclusion cap exercised
scenarios.source: 2025 IT-511 Individual Income Tax Instruction Booklet, page 21, 'Subtractions', item 1 'Retirement income': 'The maximum retirement income exclusion is $35,000 for taxpayers who are: A. 62 - 64 years of age...' Age 63 falls squarely inside that tier (this file's other three cases jump straight from below-all-tiers to above-the-top-tier, so no scenario before this one exercised the $35,000 figure). Single filer, pension income $60,000, federalAGI $60,000. Georgia standard deduction for TY2026 is $15,000 single (https://dor.georgia.gov/taxes/important-tax-updates). Georgia taxable income before exemptions = 60000-15000 = 45000. Exclusion = min(60000,35000) = 35000. Georgia taxable income = 45000-35000 = 10000. Tax = 10000*0.0499 = $499.00 (flat rate 4.99% per HB 463, https://gov.georgia.gov/press-releases/2026-05-11/gov-kemp-signs-legislation-lowering-taxes-and-supporting-economic-growth: 'HB 463 lowers Georgia's state income tax rate from 5.19% to 4.99%, beginning January 1, 2026').

scenarios.name: single, age 66, above $65,000 cap: excess retirement income is taxed
scenarios.source: Same IT-511 page 21 tier as above; age 66 is 65+, exclusion cap $65,000. Single filer, pension income $100,000, federalAGI $100,000. Georgia taxable income before exemptions = 100000-15000 = 85000 (standard deduction $15,000 single per Georgia DOR's 'Important Tax Updates' page, https://dor.georgia.gov/taxes/important-tax-updates). Exclusion = min(100000,65000) = 65000. Georgia taxable income = 85000-65000 = 20000. Tax = 20000*0.0499 = $998.00 (flat rate 4.99% per HB 463, https://gov.georgia.gov/press-releases/2026-05-11/gov-kemp-signs-legislation-lowering-taxes-and-supporting-economic-growth).

scenarios.name: MFJ, both spouses 65+ and both have their own retirement income: the per-individual doubling IS correctly configured for GA
scenarios.source: IT-511 page 21: 'The exclusion is available for the taxpayer and their spouse; however, each must qualify on a separate basis. If both spouses qualify, each spouse may claim the amounts above.' Georgia DOR's retirement-income-exclusion page (https://dor.georgia.gov/retirement-income-exclusion, dateModified 2026-01-21) states the same doubling rule more plainly: 'For married couples filing joint returns with both members receiving retirement income, the maximum adjustment for that year may be up to twice the individual exclusion amount.' Primary (age 70) has $110,000 of pension income, spouse (age 68) has $90,000; both are 65+ so each independently qualifies for the $65,000 cap, combined maximum = $130,000. federalAGI = 200000. Georgia standard deduction MFJ 2026 = $30,000 (https://dor.georgia.gov/taxes/important-tax-updates). Georgia taxable income before exemptions = 200000-30000 = 170000. Exclusion = min(200000, 65000*2) = 130000. Georgia taxable income = 170000-130000 = 40000. Tax = 40000*0.0499 = $1,996.00 (flat rate 4.99% per HB 463, https://gov.georgia.gov/press-releases/2026-05-11/gov-kemp-signs-legislation-lowering-taxes-and-supporting-economic-growth). StateTaxData.swift's GA config already sets exemptionAppliesPerIndividual: true and pensionAndIRAShareSingleCap: true, so the ENGINE correctly doubles this household's cap -- this case is a clean pass on the retirement-exclusion mechanic itself; the only defect present is the same stale rate/deduction from the two scenarios above.

scenarios.name: MFJ, only primary spouse qualifies (65+ with pension); spouse is 55 and still working
scenarios.source: Same GA mechanics as above (IT-511 page 21, 'each must qualify on a separate basis'; see also https://dor.georgia.gov/retirement-income-exclusion), but only the primary (age 66) has $70,000 of pension income and qualifies (65+); the spouse (age 55) is below the 62-64 disabled-or-tiered floor and has $50,000 of unrelated wage income, no pension of her own. Because the spouse does not independently qualify, the doubling in the previous case does not apply here, and there is no second pool of retirement income to double regardless. Exclusion = min(70000,65000) = 65000. federalAGI = 120000. Georgia standard deduction MFJ 2026 = $30,000 (https://dor.georgia.gov/taxes/important-tax-updates). Georgia taxable income before exemptions = 120000-30000 = 90000. Georgia taxable income = 90000-65000 = 25000. Tax = 25000*0.0499 = $1,247.50 (flat rate 4.99% per HB 463, https://gov.georgia.gov/press-releases/2026-05-11/gov-kemp-signs-legislation-lowering-taxes-and-supporting-economic-growth).
